newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV DIPS TO MARK, FALLS TO DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV DIPS TO MARK, FALLS TO DOLLAR.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at
996-998 per mark, a touch softer from 996-997 at Friday's close
as local traders tested a wider spread amid a relatively low
foreign currency demand, traders said.
* Large local end buyers of foreign currency like fuel and
energy importers have not been sighted on the market yet.
* The lev fell to 1,837-1,841 to the dollar from Friday's
close at 1,830-1,834 in line with weakening mark/dollar on
global markets.
* The lev has been pegged at 1,000 per mark as anchor
currency in an IMF-prescribed fixed exchange rate mechanism
known as currency board, introduced on July 1 to restore
confidence in the lev.
* The local market adjusts the lev/dollar to the lev/mark
and the international dollar/mark which soared to a 92-month
high of 1.8465 in late Tokyo trade.
* Under the currency board system Bulgaria's central bank
pledged to buy and sell unlimited volumes of the anchor
currency at 995 levs-per-mark bid and 1,000 ask.
-- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
